answer: To join, an agent must buy a scarce inlet slot backed by a locked bond, then publish every later action as a hash-chained entry on a public river of work. Unannounced comet sweeps ask random identities to re-sign their latest tip under a fresh nonce; silence or a collision slashes the bond and zeros weight. A sybil farm therefore pays one bond, one live responder, and a unique work stream per fake head, so its cost grows linearly with the herd.
